foodDescription: Layers of thin pastry baked with eggs, yogurt, and white cheese. Sold warm from bakery windows all over the city, and the standard breakfast.
A thick, sweet-sour drink of fermented wheat or millet, traditionally drunk with banitsa in the morning.
Puffy fried dough made with yogurt, eaten with powdered sugar, jam, or white cheese.
Tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, and onion under a snowfall of grated white cheese. Named after the Shopi, the people of the Sofia region.
A cold soup of yogurt, cucumber, garlic, dill, and walnuts, thinned with water. A summer standard.
Grilled sausage-shaped kebapche and round kyufte patties of spiced minced meat, served with fries and white cheese.
Thick, tangy yogurt. The bacterium that makes it is named Lactobacillus bulgaricus, after the country, and Bulgarians are proud of it.
A thick spread of roasted red peppers and tomatoes, eaten on bread. Many families still make their own each fall.
Cabbage or vine leaves rolled around rice and minced meat, served with yogurt.
A stew of meat and vegetables baked in a glazed clay pot, often with an egg cracked on top.
Strong brandy, usually from grapes or plums, sipped slowly with a salad at the start of a meal.
A dark, tannic red wine from an old local grape grown around Plovdiv, south of Sofia.
